newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open down, turn higher on U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open down, turn higher on U.S. gains.

text.p: French shares opened lower on Monday but changed direction to move higher, buoyed by Wall Street's gains on Friday.
Traders said the market was supported by the Dow's 56-point rise to a close above 7,000. Bullish brokers expect the U.S. markets to continue climbing, which should boost Paris.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.62 points at 2,715 at 1015 GMT. Volume was 875 million francs.
"The market is consolidating. Wall Street was in good form last Friday," one broker said.
Shares in Canal Plus rose 3.35 percent to 1,110 francs on market rumours the broadcaster is in talks with the Spanish government and Telefonica for a single digital television platform.
Pathe shares gained 5.29 percent to 1,493 francs on newspaper reports it could sell its BSkyB stake worth around 1.8 billion sterling.

Shares in Bollore Technologies jumped 7.66 percent to 759 francs on newspaper reports the privately-held Rivaud group was poised to cancel the double voting rights it holds in group companies, including Bollore.
Promodes shares rose 3.74 percent to 1,970 francs, extending last week's gains on the retailer's 1996 results which pleased enormously.
Societe Generale shares gained 1.44 percent to 705 francs ahead of its 1996 results due on Wednesday. One big French broker is expecting net earnings of 4.6 billion francs.
CCF shares rose 3.13 percent, joining in the rise in banking stocks, currently in favour with the stock market.
